Non-stationary environments are composed of several different stationary components (i.e., sub-environments or contexts). Therefore, algorithms that accept this assumption are incapable of learning within non-stationary environments. Reinforcement Learning - Context Detection (RL-CD) da Silva et al. (2016) method allows agents to learn the environment, detect context change points, and learn the partial model of the context without previous knowledge of the environment. RL-CD is a single-agent algorithm and it has shortcomings in learning within a multi-agent environment. In this work, we introduce a new method called Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning - Context Detection (MARL-CD), which can both detect context change points and enable agents to learn within non-stationary environments with multi-agent settings. This approach is based on RL-CD and works more effectively in terms of detecting context changes caused by agents and changes caused by the environment’s dynamics. It detects not only the change points originating from the environment, but also the change points created by the agents. Experimentally, agents spend 16% less energy compared to RL-CD and can detect change points more accurately and earlier.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4123080\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7404755\", \"title\": [\"Tracking Non-Stationary Equilibria in Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning via Evolutionary Dynamics\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Non-stationarity is a fundamental challenge in multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL).
